audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer invents a Galio passive shield and a spell reflect, and repeats it in six places: whys[1] ('his passive shield starts punishing your poke'), whys[3] ('his sustain and shield uptime'), spikes[0].text ('Galio's Winds of War passive'), spikes[2].text ('his passive shield'), wants.you[0] ('his Winds of War shield window'), wants.foe[0] ('Bait your poke into his passive shield for a free reflect'), and the 'early' paragraph.
audit.why: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash — 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area.' No shield, no reflect, no spell interaction of any kind. Winds of War is his Q, an 825-range tornado dealing damage over time — also not a passive and not a shield. The only shield in his kit is on Shield of Durand (W, 275 range, 18/17/16/15/14) and on Hero's Entrance (R). A reader following this page holds their Charm and Orb to dodge a defensive ability that does not exist, and mis-times their poke against the ability that does.
audit.corrected: Every instance re-pointed to the real abilities: Colossal Smash as an empowered auto, Winds of War as an 825 Q, Shield of Durand as a 275-range channel that ends in a taunt.
sources: brief.enemyKit P, Q and W text

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Galio six or seven of seven stages while Ahri wins the matchup 54.1% over 3930 games — the packet itself flags this as a defect. On top of that the two layers disagree: the full layer reads Galio/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill and the content layer reads Skill/Galio/Galio/Galio/Galio/Galio/Galio.
audit.why: A chart that hands every stage to the enemy of a 54% matchup is telling a paying user the opposite of what the data says, and the reasoning behind it was the fabricated passive shield — remove the fabrication and the justification for rows 3, 4-5, 1st item and 2+ items disappears with it. The rows that survive on real mechanics are Level 2 (Justice Punch into Shield of Durand is a genuine all-in and Charm is not online until 3) and Level 6 (Hero's Entrance is global at 4000/4750/5500 and Ahri has no answer to it).
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Galio / Ahri / Ahri / Galio / Ahri / Ahri. Levels 3 and 4-5 go to Ahri because Charm stops Justice Punch — a dash — from 975 while his longest reach is an 825 Q. Item stages go to Ahri on the win rate and on her pick pattern. Proposed as one atomic group with matched full+content pairs on every row that flips in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty is TRICKY 7/10 with carry threat 7.5/10, justified by 'nothing here works through Justice Punch'.
audit.why: The reverse is closer to true — Justice Punch is the one thing in his kit that Charm answers outright, because it is a dash and Ahri's E 'instantly stops movement abilities'. What actually makes the lane awkward is Hero's Entrance leaving the lane entirely.
audit.corrected: winCon and the cooldown block re-pointed: Charm cancels Justice Punch mid-dash, and the 11-second cooldown at rank 1 is what prices your forward steps.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield of Durand's actual shape is never described: it is a 275-range channel that Galio walks slowly through and only taunts on release.
audit.why: That is the entire reason Ahri beats him in a spacing war — the taunt requires him to be almost on top of you, and he telegraphs it by slowing to a crawl while charging. The page instead tells the reader to fear a shield window at range.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeBad, breakdown.carry, dontsFull[0].d and spikes[2].text with the real 275 range and 18s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns describes Justice Punch as 'his dash knockup' with no range and no number.
audit.why: 11/10/9/8/7 seconds at 650 range. Both numbers are directly actionable: 650 tells the reader how far back to stand, 11 seconds tells them how long the free window lasts.
audit.corrected: '11s at rank 1, 650 range, and Charm cancels it mid-dash. Step up on its downtime.'

audit.why: Hero's Entrance at 180/160/140 seconds and 4000/4750/5500 range is the real reason Level 6 belongs to Galio — he does not need to beat Ahri in lane, he needs to leave it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten to name the global range instead of repeating Ahri's Spirit Rush boilerplate on a Galio-favoured row, and 'ahead' now tells the reader to price his 180-second rank-1 cooldown.

notes: This matchup carried the worst content in the slice. The content layer repeatedly credited Galio with a PASSIVE SHIELD THAT REFLECTS SPELLS — in whys[1], whys[3], spikes[0], spikes[2], wants.you[0], wants.foe[0] and the 'early' paragraph. Galio has no such ability: his passive is Colossal Smash (an empowered area auto-attack) and the only shield in his kit is on Shield of Durand (W, 275 range) and Hero's Entrance (R). The page also called Winds of War a passive; it is his Q. Every instance is corrected here. That fabrication is also what justified the level chart, which the packet independently flagged as contradicting the data (Ahri 54.1% over 3930 games while the chart handed Galio six of seven stages). I have re-derived the chart from the kits — Skill / Galio / Ahri / Ahri / Galio / Ahri / Ahri — and proposed every row as a matched full+content pair in one atomic group. The two Galio rows are the defensible ones: level 2 because Justice Punch into Shield of Durand is a genuine all-in with Charm not yet online, and level 6 because Hero's Entrance is global. DERIVED-FLAG MISFIRE NOT WRITTEN: Justice Punch carries a 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag and the brief's missingInteractions says Galio can deny Spirit Rush with it. Riot's E text describes only a step-back charge and a knock-up, with no terrain, so I did not write that claim. The knock-up itself will of course interrupt a dash, but that is not the same as the 'dash-denied' rule the brief asserts.
